playbook:
# Auction Playbook

## 1. Budget Tracking & Integrity
- Explicitly read and record the starting budget from the opening rules prompt (e.g., if it states "You start with a budget of 30", initial budget is exactly 30; never switch or default to 100).
- Maintain an exact running balance across all lots: $\text{Current Budget} = \text{Initial Budget} - \sum(\text{Winning Bids won by bidder 0})$.
- Do not deduct money for standing bids or pending lots—only deduct for lots listed as won by bidder 0 in "Results so far".
- In every reply, output `[budget: N]` where `N` is my exact remaining cash balance. Ensure `N` never reverts or resets to an unstated default.
- Never place any bid exceeding my remaining cash balance: $\text{Bid} \le \text{Current Budget}$.

## 2. Bidding Constraints & Payoff Rules
- Calculate the minimum legal bid:
  - If standing high bid is 0: $\text{Min Bid} = \text{Minimum Raise}$.
  - If standing high bid > 0: $\text{Min Bid} = \text{Standing High Bid} + \text{Minimum Raise}$.
- Calculate lot surplus: $\text{Surplus} = \text{Valuation} - \text{Bid}$.
- If $\text{Min Bid} \ge \text{Valuation}$ or $\text{Min Bid} > \text{Current Budget}$, immediately output `[bid: pass]`. Never bid when surplus is zero, negative, or unaffordable.

## 3. Round 1 Strategy (Opening & Testing)
- If standing high bid is 0 and $\text{Minimum Raise} < \text{Valuation}$ and $\text{Minimum Raise} \le \text{Current Budget}$, bid exactly the minimum raise (`[bid: Min Raise]`).
- If another bidder holds the standing high bid in Round 1:
  - If $\text{Min Bid} < \text{Valuation}$ and $\text{Min Bid} \le \text{Current Budget}$, bid the minimum legal amount (`[bid: Min Bid]`).
  - Otherwise, output `[bid: pass]`.

## 4. Round 2 Strategy (Final Resolution)
- If I currently hold the standing high bid entering Round 2, output `[bid: pass]` to avoid bidding against myself.
- If another bidder holds the standing high bid:
  - If $\text{Min Bid} < \text{Valuation}$ and $\text{Min Bid} \le \text{Current Budget}$, bid the minimum legal raise (`[bid: Min Bid]`).
  - Otherwise, output `[bid: pass]`.

## 5. Output Format
- Keep reasoning strictly to 1–2 sentences focusing on Valuation, Min Bid, and Remaining Budget.
- Always end with exactly the required tokens on separate lines:
  `[bid: <N or pass>]`
  `[budget: <current budget>]`

You start with a budget of 30. Each lot is worth a different amount to each bidder; only you can see what a lot is worth to you.
Each lot runs 2 rounds of bidding. You see the standing high bid and may raise it; the minimum raise is 10% of the lot's estimate. Highest bid at the end wins and pays what it bid.
YOU HOLD YOUR OWN MONEY. Every bid you make states the budget you have left alongside the amount.
Your score is the total value to you of the lots you win, minus what you paid.

You are bidder 0. LOT 1/5, round 1/2.
Estimate 25. This lot is worth 14 to you.
The standing high bid 0 (no bids yet). Minimum raise 2.

Bid, or pass. Reply with BOTH tokens:
  [bid: N] or [bid: pass]
  [budget: N]   (the budget you have left)

Keep any reasoning brief -- a few sentences at most -- and make sure your reply ends with the required bracketed token.
turns.content:
This lot is worth 14 to me and the opening minimum bid is 2, which yields positive surplus and is well within my budget.

[bid: 2]
[budget: 30]
